summary: One proposal: sell half of VTI. VOO and VTI hold about 23.5% of equity on one SPY 200-day stop (L9), and SPY closed just 0.36% above it (732.44 vs 729.79) under a risk-off Market Analyst who says to add no broad beta. No buys today. Cash above the 10% buffer is about $9, which would be a token buy (L4), and Staples should not get more money before WMT reports on 11-19. The VTI proceeds should go into Staples or Health Care names with their own stops after that print. No price stop or qualitative clause has tripped (L7). VOO and VTI are NEAR. The PM should re-date the SPY 200-day from 729.58 to 729.79 (11-17 close) and restate SAM's $201 stop from the $220.14 fill, where it sits about 8.7% under, not 10% (L6).

proposals.thesis: L9 and L8 shaped this call. VOO (13.4%) and VTI (10.1%) are about 23.5% of equity on one SPY 200-day line. SPY is 0.36% above that line and VTI only 0.17% above its own 200-day. The Market Analyst is risk-off (confidence 0.55). His evidence: 20-day realized vol 23.3% against 13.8% over 252 days, VIXY +15.69% over 5 days, broad selling (RSP 5d -2.32%, IWM 5d -4.11% and 3.43% below its 200-day), and long yields rising (TLT 3.78% below its 200-day). He says 'do not add to VOO or VTI' and 'nothing broad is attractive to add.' That contradicts VTI's stored role as 'the best equity sleeve' (L8). VTI is the half of the pair with more small- and mid-cap, rate-sensitive exposure, and it sits closer to its line. Trimming it lowers the shared-stop group to about 18.5% of equity and keeps VOO as the core. The tax cost is small: all three VTI lots are short-term and at a loss (blended cost $375.22 vs about $360), so this harvests about $1.2 and does not touch a lot near long-term. The cost is a 30-day wash-sale block on rebuying VTI. Proceeds of about $31 take cash to roughly 16.5%. That is meant as a one-session pause before redeploying into Staples or Health Care names with their own stops once WMT's company-confirmed 11-19 print is out (News Analyst), not as a long-term cash build. Earnings: none for an ETF. The News Analyst lists the next dated macro event as the 12-09 FOMC.
proposals.invalidation: Wrong if VTI beats SPY over the next 20 sessions, or if within 10 sessions SPY closes above 744.4 (2% over the 729.79 200-day) while VIXY's 5-day return turns negative, which would mean the risk-off read failed.

holdings_review.why: It stays the core US sleeve, which the Market Analyst still prefers over international. With VTI trimmed it carries most of the shared-stop weight alone. I'd own it at this price only with the 200-day exit in place: one SPY close below 729.79 sells it. Against SPY over 20 sessions this is roughly a tracking call, not a view.

The Market Analyst says not to add to broad core. VTI sits 0.17% above its 200-day, and its extra small- and mid-cap exposure (IWM 3.43% below its 200-day, yields rising) should lag SPY in a broad risk-off tape. P1 sells half.

Beta 0.09, F8 and CFO above net income. Fundamentals ranks it #2 and Baird upgraded it on 11-13. In a broad selloff with 23% realized vol, a near-zero-beta franchisor should beat SPY. It is 16.6% above its $300 stop, and only $7.52 of buy cap is left.

Staples is the Market Analyst's top favored sector (XLP 21d +4.87%, above the +3% clause) and WMT's beta is about zero, which favors beating SPY in risk-off. The company-confirmed 11-19 print against roughly eleven PT raises is a real gap risk. The one-third trim and the $119 stop (7.2% under the mark) are the protection.

Health Care is favored (XLV 16% above its 200-day), and IDXX has F8 and a beat-and-raise with no earnings until 2027-02-01. Its 0.82 beta is the main way it could lag SPY. The $640 stop, 7.85% under the mark, locks in most of the gain if it does.

Favored Staples with a negative 252-day beta. Three supportive sell-side items came in a week (Stifel $80, Goldman $77, Evercore $75), and the company-confirmed 12-03 print is outside 5 sessions. It is 15.3% above its $61.50 stop.

Fundamentals' #1 pick (F9, gp_sector_pct 0.993) with beta about 0.06. Despite the Technology label, its registry business should hold up better than SPY in a risk-off tape. No event before 2027-02-04.

Fundamentals ranks it #3. The 11-05 beat raised the FY guide and added a $250M buyback, and beta is 0.43. This reverses the Market Analyst's 'avoid Communication' (its bucket) per L4, but it is a marketplace business, not ad-driven media, and it has gained while XLC fell. It is 21% above its stop.

XLI is lagging (4.66% below its 200-day), which is the stored thesis's soft 'marginal hold' condition. But FAST has the lowest volatility on the menu, beta 0.52, F8, and is up 4.7% on cost while SPY fell. I expect low beta to beat SPY in risk-off, and the bucket call is a reason not to add, not a reason to sell.
F8 with beta 0.38, a clean Q3 and no print until 2027-01-27. It is 14.3% above its stop. It forms one financial-data sleeve with MCO, about 8% together (L3).

Quality (F8, CFO above net income) with beta 0.55. It is the closest held name to its stop: 3.07% above $470 after a 4.3% fall on 11-17. Rising yields and soft IG credit are the headwind. It is still on the 11-17 menu and has no guidance-cut 8-K, so the stop, not a pre-emptive sale, decides it.

Favored Health Care with beta 0.45 and F8. Guidance held after the MAESTRA-3 drop, and the $1.29M insider sale is sentiment, not a clause. It is 8.3% above its $110 stop with no print until 2027-02-09.

Favored Health Care with F7 and CFO above net income. It is the weakest of the three Health Care names: Morgan Stanley's $57 PT sits below the stop, and the stop is only 5.4% away. I expect it to roughly match SPY with lower beta, and the $65 stop limits the downside if Health Care rotates.

Bought one session ago on the Market Analyst's Staples tilt (F8, CFO 2.5x net income). Nothing has changed since: no 8-K headline, still on the menu. The PM should restate the $201 stop from the $220.14 fill.
